brief: Friday's session accelerated the AI-stock selloff: the S&P 500 posted a seventh consecutive down session, the Nasdaq had its worst week since 2020 (-10.4%), and MSCI EM entered a bear market, down 21% from its June peak, its worst weekly drop since March 2020. US futures opened sharply higher overnight. The question is whether Friday's lows mark a floor or a pause. The clearest relief has come from bonds: the flight-to-quality bid pushed 10-year UST yields down 20bps on the week, and markets have moved to deprice Fed tightening, though the note separately states markets price about 94% odds of a further 25bp hike at the December 9 FOMC meeting. This week's PMIs today and Wednesday's US core PCE are called key. Asian markets showed tentative stabilization after governments rolled out emergency measures. Kospi still fell 3.3%, while CSI 300, Hang Seng and Taiex pared early losses. Credit spreads widened broadly, with tech names (SpaceX, Oracle, Nvidia) hit hardest in CDS following Anthropic. Metals sold off except energy. European corporate bond issuance, driven by hyperscalers, topped €2 trillion for the first time.
